It's incredibly fun and addictive honestly even though some of the ramp ups in levels are insane and pisses me off at times it's extremely relaxing and just a good game to get on if you're looking for something to do.

Slay the Spire relies heavily on luck. Two runs can be similar but aren't the same. There's a lot riding on your first Act because it doesn't matter what build you want to play, there's either going to be a build you get to play or a death if you don't make it come together. Along with deck order being pre-determined as a fight starts(a wise move to prevent save scumming, just noting the mechanic) it's a management game long term more than anything. In order to be truly good at the game, you need hours and hours and dozens and dozens of runs for true progress. Because the game is geared on that it really feels more like I'm zoning out hoping for a good run or managing a dead run mid to late game. While it does excel at small rewards to keep the player invested including progress on death I won't pretend it's a style of gameplay I'm super into. But for it's genre I think it's done very well.

This isn't my genre but I think it excels at what it wants and if you get it on sale specifically you'll be pleased for at least your first dozens runs.

Tips and tricks for the interested:

-Large decks are usually a trap, burying the best cards or your intended build under energy wasters. 15-20 cards or less is my advice

-I almost always try to gun for Events and Rests over Elites after Act 1

-During Rests, if you can, I'd recommend upgrading cards. Specifically any beyond the basic Defense and Attack you start with

-Avoid bias with your deck and adapt. Re-evaluating even endgame can help win your fights, and never expect to get the exact build you are looking for

This is probably one of the best games I have played in recent years. 
There is great replayability because each time is always different and you can't really apply the same strategy in every run. 
The premise is simple and easy to pick up, but you'll realise soon that the game runs really deep after you play for a while. 
This is a great game for someone who likes strategy and wants a challenge more than a point & click game or a visual novel. But if you are anything like me, I'm sure you will get hooked by this game just 30mins into playing!

Defect is the goat!!
:sts_defect:

Defect is my favorite character in Slay The Spire. His move set and unique mechanic are really amazing. Being able to channel four different types of orb is really amazing, allowing the character to have very diverse builds except for the Plasma orb. You can either choose Frost, Lightning, or Dark as your main build, but i mainly use the Frost or Lightning cause i dont like using the dark orb. Even though, its idea of dealing more damage the longer its channeled is good and can be very destructive, but i enjoy more of the lightning. Lightning is like one of the best or might even be the best orb to channel. With some specific power cards, you can endlessly channel and evoke orbs, dealing massive damage, and the more focus you have the more overpowered you are. (but ig every character with specific insane cards can be unkillable and being able to one shot most bosses) 
Ngl Defect is a fun character to play with and needs a ton of strategy like not knowing what cards to pick and what not to, receiving cards that actively makes your deck worse, or finding yourself stuck with random cards that have no synergy with each other at all.
